anchors.paper_title: Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding
anchors.reason: The candidate paper title, 'Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding,' directly matches the dataset's topic and authors, suggesting it is the primary publication describing the data.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded from 128 channels with a 10x preamp gain and converted to Volts (×1e-6). Participants performed speech production tasks under three conditions (overt, minimally overt, covert) producing one of five color words. Each trial consisted of 5 repetitions of the same word lasting 1.25 seconds per repetition. Additional channels recorded EOG, EMG from upper and lower orbicularis oris muscles, microphone input, and trial onset triggers. Data collection included both offline calibration sessions for decoder training and online sessions with real-time decoding.

citation_details.title: Delineating neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding
citation_details.author: Motoshige Sato, Yasuo Kabe, Sensho Nobe, Akito Yoshida, Masakazu Inoue, Mayumi Shimizu, Kenichi Tomeoka, Shuntaro Sasai
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises 128-channel EEG recordings acquired during speech production tasks involving overt, minimally overt, and covert speech conditions. Participants produced one of five color words, with each trial consisting of five repetitions. The dataset includes calibration and online real-time decoding sessions, along with supplementary physiological recordings (EOG, EMG, microphone) and trigger markers, designed to investigate neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding.
